question: Issuing verbal preparation instructions alone is sufficient for most imaging procedures, because patients can remember what they are told in a clinical consultation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Verbal instructions alone are not sufficient. Patient recall after verbal counselling is poor, particularly in anxious patients. Always provide BOTH verbal explanation (to confirm understanding and answer questions) AND written instructions (for the patient to refer to at home before the procedure).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Verbal instructions alone are insufficient. Patients frequently forget or misremember verbal-only instructions, especially for complex or anxiety-provoking procedures. Written instructions serve as a durable reference and should accompany verbal counselling for every imaging procedure.
